scenario_text: A metallic sample is cooled below its transition temperature and its electrical resistance drops as scattering channels freeze out. Experimenters measure the residual electrical resistivity at various temperatures in the low-temperature regime where lattice vibration contributions dominate. Each measurement is an independent equilibrium reading of resistivity at a fixed bath temperature. The goal is to relate the measured resistivity to temperature and the density of scattering centers.
